body:
Hi maintainers! I'd like to contribute to this issue.

I'm comfortable with JavaScript, Node.js, and backend development, and I'd be interested in investigating this issue and contributing a focused fix with regression tests.

Would you be open to a community contribution? If so, could you please confirm whether this issue is still relevant and whether I can work on it?

I'll wait for your guidance before starting implementation. Thanks!

Some follow-up data, since I had the reproduction to hand.

I ran the repro from the issue body against every Fastify major back to 4.0.0 (Node 22.23.2, one clean install per version). Two things came out of it, and the first corrects my own report.

**The halting behaviour has never differed.** I described this as 5.12.5 behaviour because that is what we were running. It is identical back to 4.0.0: replying from an async `preHandler` stops the chain with zero or one async `onSend` hooks registered, and does not with two or more. Not a 5.x regression.

**The symptom changed at 5.11.0, and that boundary is the interesting part.**

| fastify | halts at 0–1 hooks | halts at 2–3 hooks | process exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.0.0, 4.28.1 | yes | **no** | **1 — uncaught `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`** |
| 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0, 5.9.0, 5.10.0 | yes | **no** | **1 — same throw** |
| **5.11.0**, 5.12.0, 5.12.5 | yes | **no** | 0 — silent |

Up to and including 5.10.0, the handler writing to an already-sent reply threw out of a promise and terminated the process:

```
Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot write headers after they are sent to the client
    at onSendEnd (/node_modules/fastify/lib/reply.js:493:7)
    at wrapOnSendEnd (/node_modules/fastify/lib/reply.js:435:5)
    at next (/node_modules/fastify/lib/hooks.js:213:7)
    at handleResolve (/node_modules/fastify/lib/hooks.js:230:5)
```

From 5.11.0 that throw is gone, the chain still runs, and the status code is just overwritten.

So between those versions a crash became a silently wrong status code. That is the whole reason this survived in our production: the only remaining trace was one route answering `400` with a `401` body.

I am not claiming 5.11.0 introduced a bug — suppressing that throw looks like a reasonable fix on its own. It may be that whoever made it did not know the chain was still running underneath.

Happy to open a PR, but I would rather not guess which half is the intended behaviour: should two or more async `onSend` hooks be able to change whether an async `preHandler` reply halts the chain, or is the documented halt the contract and the hook count irrelevant? Point me at the intended semantics and I will write it.
